children: Our Bureau Mumbai: IndiGo and Akasa Air have extended flight cancellations to Saudi Arabia amid continuing security concerns in the Middle East, with IndiGo keeping its Riyadh services suspended until October 31 and flights to three other Saudi cities cancelled until October 27.
The extensions affect services to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah, key destinations for Indian travellers and workers.

The disruptions come amid attacks on Saudi targets, raising concerns over the safety of airport operations and prompting airlines to reassess their schedules. In a travel advisory on Friday, IndiGo said flights to and from Riyadh would remain cancelled until October 31 (inclusive), while services to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah would remain suspended until October 27 (inclusive).

The airline said it was monitoring developments and coordinating with the relevant authorities. Affected passengers are being notified through their contact details and have been advised to check their flight status before leaving for the airport. Akasa Air had earlier, on October 18, extended the suspension of all flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until October 27. The airline is offering affected passengers a full refund, credited to the original payment source within seven days, or rescheduling without an additional charge.

Air India and Air India Express had also suspended operations to Saudi Arabia amid the security situation. The disruptions follow attacks on Saudi targets earlier this month, including an attack at Riyadh airport that killed an Indian national and injured several others.

title: IndiGo, Akasa Air Extend Saudi Flight Cancellations
